newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- SING TAO -- Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa held an official meeting with Koo Chen-fu, head of Taiwan's Straits Exchange Foundation. A formal and new communication channel would soon be set up.

-- HONG KONG DAILY NEWS -- About 500 illegal immigrant children gathered at the Immigration Department to apply for SAR identity cards. The department said the children would not be sent back to the mainland until background checks were complete.

-- MING PAO -- Solicitor General Daniel Fung said the legal department had started working on a new election law, which was expected to be completed by the end of the month. It said the first SAR legislature election would be held in March next year.

-- Analysts said Xinhua News Agency's statement that it would no longer act as China's spokesperson in Hong Kong showed the agency's role in the territory had started to change, which would be good for the SAR governemnt to operate independently.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- The SAR government started its operation on Thursday. Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa inspected different departments and said that it ws a good start.

-- WEN WEI PO -- The head of Xinhua News Agency's Hong Kong branch, Zhou Nan, said that the task of reunification had entered a new era, and Hong Kong's return was a milestone in the development of the Chinese nation.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Local hotels' occupancy rate dropped dramatically after the handover, some falling below 50 per cent. The Hong Kong Tourist Association said that the number of tourists during the handover was lower than expected.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The SAR government would soon announce land sales for the next 21 months and the land supply in the three years that followed. Financial Secretary Donald Tsang pointed out that Hong Kong had no potential to expand physically, and therefore, the demand for land was urgent.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Police Commissioner Eddie Hui had ordered senior officers not to use national security as a reason to ban demonstrations and public processions without the direct approval of the Director of Operations.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Dharmala Holdings, one of the largest conglomerates in Indonesia, had forged a strategic alliance with Guangdong Investments that would likely serve as a vehicle for the Indonesion group to strengthen and expand its investments in the SAR and China.
